# Now 2.10.71
- Fixed the blank cover that appeared while swiping forward in Apple Music. - Next-track previews now come from Apple Music's resolved native Up Next queue, with the exact embedded artwork, instead of incorrectly treating the full Music library as the queue. - Stale queue responses are rejected when their current-track identity no longer matches the overlay. - When a queue preview is genuinely unavailable, the current cover now responds elastically instead of sliding away into a blank tile.

# Now 2.10.70
- Fixed Check for Updates incorrectly reporting “up to date” when GitHub's raw-file CDN served a stale appcast. - Update checks now use the no-cache latest-release feed, with the previous release refreshed as a safe redirect fallback. - Publishing now reads the prior feed directly from GitHub's origin API and verifies the exact URL embedded in installed clients before declaring success. - Includes Apple Music previous/next artwork previews for album and playlist playback from 2.10.69.

# Now 2.10.69
- Apple Music album and playlist playback now previews the real previous or next cover while you swipe, using the track's exact embedded artwork. - Adjacent covers are prefetched in both directions and handed directly into the completed skip, preventing a duplicate artwork transition. - Playlist position is validated before every preview; first/last-track boundaries do not show stale artwork. - Shuffled and opaque streaming queues decline speculative next artwork because macOS does not expose their resolved Up Next order. - When Apple Music hides its queue, the previous cover still uses verified playback history instead of an unrelated playlist guess.
